name: Critical-regime XY Monte Carlo schedules
description: schedule(temperature, lattice_size, budget) -> list of 1..64 kernel names: metropolis, overrelax, wolff, containing a stochastic kernel. Trusted detailed-balance kernels operate classical periodic XY model. Each sweep/cluster is charged N site units (upper bound); warmup counts. Multiple independent chains score squared energy/magnetization errors against long independent reference chains, with reference uncertainty and autocorrelation diagnostics. Fixed-work local adaptation, not a timing leaderboard.

papers.title: Collective Monte Carlo Updating for Spin Systems
papers.task_relation: The local task schedules trusted Metropolis, overrelaxation, and Wolff kernels for finite XY systems under a work budget. It optimizes a restricted mixture of existing kernels; its schedule search and equilibrium-error score are not the paper's new cluster algorithm.
papers.primary_goal: Improve equilibrium Monte Carlo sampling near criticality through collective spin-cluster updates, including the XY model.

science_relevance.scientific_problem: Sample critical spin-model equilibria efficiently despite long autocorrelation times.
science_relevance.importance_rationale: Reducing critical slowing in physical spin-system sampling is the main goal of the Wolff algorithm paper.
science_relevance.reason: The primary target is efficient physical equilibrium sampling. The local schedule is explicitly an adaptation of that research problem.
